title: fix(approvals): the stranded-request inspection keeps finding new strands past 500 decided requests
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuRzPnJEdqn6ymW4qaMMQS69)_

Fixes #37808

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

Related: #37767, ADR-0162

## 维护者速读

- 是什么：审批插件每 5 分钟会自动检查一次「已经批了、但后续流程走不下去」的审批请求，并写日志提醒管理员。以前它每次只随便取 500 条已决请求，已决请求超过 500 条后，新出问题的那条可能一直轮不到。现在每次先看最新的 500 条，再按顺序轮着看后面的 500 条，所有已决请求都会被定期看到。
- 为什么：#37767（关闭态锁定）之后，管理员要靠这个检查发现卡住的单据，它不能漏报。
- 出错会怎样：只是个只读的检查，只写日志，不改任何数据；每次多读最多 500 行。可直接撤回。
- 要你做的：无，座位复核即可。

## What happens on `main`

`#inspectStrandedRequests` rides the five-minute approvals sweep. It read `limit` (500) rows of every `approved` / `rejected` / `returned` request with **no order and no cursor**. Past 500 decided requests the page is whatever the store hands back (SQLite: insertion order), so a request stranded today, behind 500 older decisions, was never inspected on any sweep.

**Reproduced first** (main `a8396da1`, then rebased on `94b0314c` after #37925 merged; real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver`, better-sqlite3 in memory, so order and filters are the store's):

| Test | `main` | this PR |
|:--|:--|:--|
| CONTROL: 50 healthy decided requests + 1 strand: reported | green | green |
| 600 healthy decided requests + 1 strand decided last: reported on the first sweep | **red** (`[]`) | green |
| 1,200 healthy + 1 strand that is the oldest decision with the highest id: reported within one pass of the walk (sweep 3), and again on the next pass (sweep 6) | **red** (never) | green |

## What changes

`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts#inspectStrandedRequests` reads two windows of at most `limit` rows, each filtered and ordered by the store (Prime Directive 5: no in-app scan):

1. **The newest decisions:** `where status ∈ strandable, orderBy updated_at desc, id desc, limit`, on the existing `(status, updated_at)` index. A decision whose run could not advance (the request's `updated_at` is set when it is decided) is reported on the next sweep.
2. **The next page of a walk over every decided request by id:** `where status ∈ strandable [and id > cursor], orderBy id asc, limit`. The cursor (`strandScanCursor`, an instance field) is the last id the previous sweep read; a page shorter than `limit` resets it, so the walk starts again.

Rows of the second window already in the first are dropped; `scanned` counts distinct rows. Everything after the read (the three oracles, the mirror read, the log line, the result shape) is unchanged.

### Why this shape cannot miss a strand

- The walk is a keyset on the primary key. An id never changes, and a row that leaves the strandable set (or one that is added) moves no other row's key, so no row is skipped. Every decided request is read at least once every `ceil(decided / limit)` sweeps.
- That covers the two cases the newest window alone would miss: more than `limit` decisions between two sweeps, and a run that fails after its decision (the request row is not updated then, so it does not come back into the newest window).
- The newest window keeps the common case fast: a strand made at decision time is reported on the next sweep, not at the end of a pass.
- A restart drops the cursor, so the walk starts again from the first id: a repeat, never a miss.

**Ablations** (fix committed first, restored from `HEAD` after each):
- `approval-service.ts` back to `main` → the two >500 pins red (2 failed / 37 passed).
- newest window only (walk removed) → the old-strand pin red (1 / 38).
- walk only (newest window removed) → the new-strand pin red (1 / 38).

## Decided in the thread (small, listed per the standing rule)

- **No store-filterable mark.** A column marking "may be stranded" would add a field to `sys_approval_request` (a platform object, so `Clause-②: yes`) and a writer on every path that can strand a request. The two ordered windows need neither.
- **Each window takes `limit`.** A sweep reads at most 2 × 500 rows instead of 500, and makes at most twice as many oracle calls. Halving each window would halve how fast the walk covers a large deployment; I kept the per-window size at the existing default.
- **The cursor lives in memory.** It is not persisted, because losing it only restarts the walk. Each process of a cluster walks independently.
- **`updated_at`, not `completed_at`,** for the newest window: it is the column the existing `(status, updated_at)` index covers, and a decision sets both.
- **Pin location:** a new top-level `describe` in the existing harness file `stranded-request-inspection.test.ts`, on a real SQL engine (the file's fake engine ignores order), with a fresh in-memory store per test.
- **Docs:** `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`, the paragraph on the read-only inspection, says which rows a sweep reads.

## Gates run locally (worktree on `94b0314c` + this diff)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals test`: 131 files, 1979 tests passed
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck` (incl. `check:test-typecheck`): pass
- `eslint` on the two touched source files: clean
